audit_findings.title: The anchor uses a partial-year acquisition perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed full-perimeter 2025 pro forma revenue was $229.123 million above reported revenue, while pro forma net income was $22.869 million lower; owner-earnings impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor OE reflects seven months of Helly Hansen operations, while acquisition financing and the balance-sheet bridge reflect the acquired business; this affects normalized OE and every forecast year.
audit_findings.evidence: The acquisition of Helly Hansen was completed on May 31, 2025, and the results of operations have been included in our consolidated financial statements since that date.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but its direction in owner earnings is unresolved because twelve-month operating profit, interest expense, maintenance investment and working capital can offset one another. The filed pro forma results show a large enough change to alter scenario values, so the transition-year anchor is not decision-ready.
audit_findings.action: Build a twelve-month, same-perimeter OE reconciliation for Helly Hansen, including acquisition debt interest, maintenance capex and normalized working capital, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The stakes bridge may gross up assets pledged economically to deferred-compensation claims
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $55.222 million potential bridge overstatement, or $0.97 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: If the $51.717 million investment assets are in stakes_net, the associated $55.222 million deferred-compensation liability must also enter the equity bridge; netting would reduce the current bridge by $55.222 million.
audit_findings.evidence: These investment securities and earnings thereon are intended to provide a source of funds to meet the deferred compensation obligations, and serve as an economic hedge of the financial impact of changes in deferred compensation liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The economic matching of the investments and liabilities is demonstrated, but their inclusion in stakes_net is not. The potential adjustment is about 1.5% of base equity value and would reduce the bull value from $74.77 to approximately $73.80 per share. It would not reverse the current no-buy conclusion but could affect the near-fair bull-case interpretation.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $92.8 million stakes_net ledger components and rerun the bridge after excluding both matched amounts or deducting the full current and noncurrent deferred-compensation liabilities.

audit_findings.title: The China joint venture may be counted in both owner earnings and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $39.270 million bridge amount ($0.69 per share), or a computed $64.4-$89.7 million operating-PV effect ($1.13-$1.58 per share) if the filed $5.411 million equity-method income is purged
audit_findings.mechanism: The joint venture may enter value through both equity-method income in anchor OE and its investment carrying amount in stakes_net.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company reports its 50 % of the joint venture's profits and losses as "Income from equity method investment", a separate component of net income within the statements of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates both a $39.270 million investment and $5.411 million of equity-method income, but the supplied record does not prove that both entered the valuation. If they did, the duplication is large enough under the income-purge treatment to move the $74.77 bull value below the $73.59 market price.
audit_findings.action: Identify every stakes_net component and the anchor treatment of equity-method income; rerun once with income retained and the stake excluded, and once with income purged and the stake separately valued.

audit_findings.title: Receivables sales can make operating cash flow look like owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $83.2 million increase in outstanding sold receivables, equal to 33.8% of anchor OE; if fully embedded, computed value sensitivity is $989.7-$1,379.4 million or $17.38-$24.22 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional receivables sold converts working capital into operating cash flow and can inflate a CFO-derived OE anchor without representing recurring earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 2025 and December 2024, $ 261.4 million and $ 178.2 million, respectively, of the sold trade accounts receivable remained outstanding with the financial institutions under these agreements.
audit_findings.explanation: The $83.2 million financing-balance increase is demonstrated; whether the OE calculation reversed it is unresolved. Its possible scale is plainly capable of changing every valuation scenario and the buy-below conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile anchor-year operating cash flow to receivables sold, deferred purchase-price assets and collections; reverse the financing-driven change attributable to the valued perimeter and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A purchase-price hedge gain is nonrecurring
audit_findings.magnitude: $24.1 million pre-tax; at the filed 24.3% effective tax rate, computed indicative after-tax amount is $18.244 million with $217.0-$302.5 million or $3.81-$5.31 per-share value sensitivity
audit_findings.mechanism: If included in anchor OE, the acquisition-specific gain is projected and capitalized through the operating DCF and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: During the first and second quarters of 2025, the Company entered into foreign currency exchange contracts totaling $ 1.3 billion CAD to hedge the purchase price of the Acquisition, which were settled on May 30, 2025, for a gain of $ 24.1 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The gain's nonrecurring nature is demonstrated, but its inclusion in OE is not. The filing classifies the settlement proceeds as investing cash flow, which would normally keep them out of CFO-based OE, yet no OE reconciliation confirms that treatment. If included, the adjustment is sufficient to move the bull value below the market price.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE reconciliation for the full $24.1 million gain and its actual tax effect; remove only the purchase-price hedge result and rerun all scenarios if any amount remains.

audit_findings.title: Project Jeanius costs should not be stripped as completed one-offs
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed restructuring and transformation charges were $80.6 million in 2025, equal to 32.7% of anchor OE, versus $38.3 million in 2024; the OE add-back is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding recurring transformation cash costs back to OE while forecasting related savings inflates the anchor and capitalizes an asymmetric normalization.
audit_findings.evidence: We anticipate to incur additional costs associated with Project Jeanius as we continue to execute on this multi-year initiative.
audit_findings.explanation: The multi-year and continuing nature of Project Jeanius expenditures is demonstrated, including management's expectation of additional costs. Whether and how much was added back to the $246.4 million anchor remains unresolved. The filed charge scale is readily capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every acquisition, restructuring and transformation adjustment in OE, separating cash from noncash items; retain recurring execution costs and rerun after allowing only evidenced nonrecurring cash add-backs.
